units.function: Pure route-authorization tests for Company read/write access across board users, viewers, instance admins, local implicit operators, Agent actors and Agents acting on behalf of a responsible human.
units.dependencyDirection: Actor middleware supplies user/Agent identity, Company ids, membership snapshots and deployment-source flags; route helpers derive boolean visibility or throw HTTP errors before services execute, while organization-level board access uses a broader membership-or-instance-admin predicate.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent/none actor, source, Company id, active membership and viewer/operator role, instance-admin flag, onBehalfOfUserId and responsible-user membership snapshot, HTTP read/write method and structured denial code.
units.lifecycle: Active viewers may read but not write; detailed membership snapshots override legacy Company-id lists. Session instance admins cannot enter a Company without membership, while local_implicit board identity can. Agents are confined to their Company and delegated writes are capped by an active non-viewer responsible human; absent/read-only snapshots fail closed unless a global shadow-mode environment switch converts denial into logging only.
units.testAssessment: Nineteen focused cases cover read/write role behavior, legacy compatibility, local mode, responsible-human ceiling, boolean/assert parity and organization-level access. Missing are suspended/expired/duplicate memberships, membership version or revocation during a run, method override/WebSocket/background jobs, route-level policy composition, shadow-mode audit verification, deployment-profile misconfiguration, accountable purpose and property/action-level permissions. Tests also codify two broad bypasses: legacy companyIds-only writes and local_implicit all-Company access.
units.designRationale: Centralize coarse tenant isolation, preserve older actor shapes, support frictionless local operation and progressively roll out responsible-user authorization without immediately breaking existing Agent flows.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires identity-provider-neutral tenant isolation and a mandatory accountable-human authority ceiling that remains valid through long-running Agent work in managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a versioned authorization decision port with explicit Principal, MembershipGrant, ResponsibilityContract, action/resource/purpose and policy revision. Preserve fail-closed responsible-human checks and read-only viewers. Restrict local bootstrap to a named instance owner and explicit organizations; remove production legacy actor fallback and never permit a global shadow switch to bypass high-risk enforcement.
units.responsibilityConflict: The accountable-human ceiling is optional under PAPERCLIP_RESPONSIBLE_USER_AUTHZ_SHADOW, legacy board actors can write from companyIds without role detail, and local_implicit identity receives unrestricted Company access. Membership snapshots carry no policy version, expiry or proof that authority remained valid when an Agent later executes.

units.function: Repository-static regression test intended to require a tenant-visibility 404 gate before write authorization on resources looked up by id, preventing 403-versus-404 cross-tenant existence disclosure.
units.dependencyDirection: The test scans first-party route source text at test time, matches direct assertCompanyAccess(req, variable.companyId) calls, searches the previous twelve lines for a corresponding hasCompanyAccess call and exempts two request-input sites through a manually maintained allowlist.
units.keyDataModels: Route filename/source line, resource variable and companyId expression, twelve-line lookback window, request-input allowlist entry and 404 visibility-before-403 mutation pattern.
units.lifecycle: Every test run enumerates TypeScript route files and reports recognized assertion sites without a nearby visibility gate. A companion test rejects allowlist entries whose exact assertion expression disappeared.
units.testAssessment: The two tests provide useful cheap regression coverage and stale-allowlist hygiene, but the regex recognizes only one-line direct calls with a word variable and literal .companyId. Aliases, destructuring, multiline calls, wrappers, optional chaining, renamed helpers, non-route transports and gates more than twelve lines away can evade or falsely trigger it; it proves source shape, not runtime 404 behavior or query-level tenant filtering.
units.designRationale: Institutionalize a subtle tenant-enumeration fix across many route handlers without requiring each contributor to remember the pattern manually.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must prevent cross-tenant existence, timing and count oracles consistently across REST, events, search, export, Connector and realtime boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the invariant structurally: tenant-scope repository queries by construction, expose findVisibleById rather than global getById, use typed authorization middleware, add runtime black-box cross-tenant suites and optionally an AST rule. Retain a narrowly documented exception ledger with owners and expiry, not regex source scanning as the primary control.
units.responsibilityConflict: A source-shape guard can be green while an alias, alternate helper or non-HTTP path leaks another Company's resource. Responsibility evidence itself is sensitive, so existence protection must apply to every projection and event subscription rather than only recognized route assertions.

units.function: Unit tests for projecting the authenticated actor and intended technical consumer into SecretService access-event context without injecting binding or configuration-path authority.
units.dependencyDirection: Route code supplies the trusted Express actor plus consumer type/id; buildActorSecretContext maps board users or delegated Agents to actor and responsible-user attribution, then SecretService performs any later resolution and binding checks.
units.keyDataModels: Actor type/id/source, userId, onBehalfOfUserId, responsibleUserId, consumerType agent/environment/system, consumerId, deliberately absent configPath and allowedBindingIds.
units.lifecycle: Board user identity becomes both actor and responsible human. Agent identity remains the actor while its on-behalf-of human becomes responsible; direct userId wins if both fields exist. Missing human responsibility remains null. Caller-selected consumer attribution passes through, but no binding allowlist or path is minted by this helper.
units.testAssessment: Five compact cases cover attribution precedence, absent human responsibility, all consumer classes and absence of accidental binding fields. Missing are actor type/source validation, spoof-resistant construction, consumer ownership/tenant matching, required responsible human by purpose, grants, Work/action/purpose, Secret version, expiry, decision/evidence linkage and integration proving access is denied rather than merely logged when context is incomplete.
units.designRationale: Separate honest audit attribution from Secret binding authorization and avoid fabricating configuration scope at the HTTP edge.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs every Secret projection to identify the actual requester, accountable human and execution consumer while proving a purpose-bound grant to a specific Work action and data policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the separation of actor, responsible human and consumer, plus the rule that route helpers cannot invent binding authority. Replace free consumer parameters with a validated Connector/ExecutionPrincipal reference and require SecretGrant id/version, Work/action digest, purpose, expiry, data contract and accountable human before issuance; null responsibility must fail for governed use.
units.responsibilityConflict: The context is attribution metadata, not authorization. Callers choose consumerType/id, responsibility may be null and no grant/binding/action scope is carried, so an access event can truthfully describe a technically successful use that was never organizationally authorized.
